title: Metrics lab
description: Move the fraud model's threshold, or type your own counts, and watch accuracy, precision, recall, F1 and the business cost change.
intro: Cairnway's fraud model gives each of 1,000 test orders a score from 0 to 1, and orders at or above the threshold are held for review. 50 of the orders really are fraud. Move the threshold all the way up, so nothing is flagged, and look at the accuracy. Then lower it and watch precision and recall pull in opposite directions.
takeaways: Precision asks: when the model says fraud, how often is it right? TP / (TP + FP). Recall asks: of all real fraud, how much did it catch? TP / (TP + FN).
With rare events, accuracy misleads: flagging nothing scores 95% accuracy here and catches no fraud at all.

Lowering the threshold raises recall and lowers precision; raising it does the opposite. Missed cases are costly (fraud, disease): favour recall. False alarms are costly (blocking good customers): favour precision.
F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall: one balanced number when both matter and the classes are unbalanced.
The best model metric is not always the best business result. Business metrics such as cost, ROI and customer feedback decide whether a model is worth running.
